A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MANU research work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison; v2 retains the original material and adds appendix experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original unlearning experiments on LLaVA-1.5-7B and Idefics2-8B, including baseline comparisons, pruning-ratio analyses, and utility evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds utility-benchmark evaluations, importance-function ablations, and LLaVA-13B experiments in Tables 6–8.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the four importance functions, their sum, the forget/retain importance ratio, and selective weight zeroing. The new component-removal experiments test variants without changing the proposed MANU procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix E.5 substantially broadens downstream utility coverage through MIA-Bench conversational evaluation, MM-Vet integrated multimodal reasoning, and MMStar vision-indispensable tasks. The original MLLMU-Bench, MMMU, and LLaVA-Bench evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain their comparator membership. Table 8 extends GA, Gradient Difference, KL Minimization, Prompting, and NPO to LLaVA-13B; Table 6 reuses GA, Gradient Difference, KL Minimization, and NPO on the added benchmarks. No new competing unlearning algorithm is introduced.

E3.justification: The additions introduce a 13B model configuration and controls that zero one importance function at a time. Tables 6–8 use the 5% forget setting. Original splits, metrics, and procedures remain unchanged; Table 8 does not specify the pruning ratio despite its caption mentioning varying ratios.

E4.justification: v1 analyzes pruning ratios, modality imbalance, and utility tradeoffs. Appendix E.6 and Table 7 add systematic removal of each of the four importance functions on both original model architectures, directly testing component contributions that v1 did not experimentally isolate.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional tables continue reporting point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–5 and figure results remain unchanged. Tables 6–8 add utility scores, ablation outcomes, and 13B results: for example, LLaVA MIA-Bench scores are 64.02 for MANU versus 63.44 for NPO, and LLaVA-13B MANU forget classification accuracy is 33.65%. Table 7 also introduces unexplained Idefics2 cloze values that conflict with retained Tables 4–5.

T1.justification: The importance-function definitions, scoring and pruning equations, and baseline objectives are unchanged. The added empirical interpretations introduce no mathematical definitions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about modality-aware pruning, balanced unlearning, and utility preservation. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E.6 adds interpretations assigning forgetting benefits to frequency/variance importance and utility preservation to absolute/RMS importance. It argues for complementary signals while acknowledging that tuned weights could improve results. E.7 adds an interpretation of transfer to larger models; Section 8's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E.7 newly documents separately fine-tuning a vanilla LLaVA-13B model on MLLMU-Bench. Existing batch-size, hardware, baseline implementation, and code-access information remains unchanged, with little additional implementation detail for the new experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for MIA-Bench, MM-Vet, and MMStar, plus introductory citations to Wang et al. (2024b) and Zhang et al. (2025b). Section 6's related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Appendix E.5–E.7 and updates the Section 5.3 appendix reference. Existing prose and section order are largely retained, with limited reflow and citation-related edits.

P2.justification: Tables 6–8 add three appendix displays using the established table style. Original Tables 1–5 and all twelve figures are retained; appendix floats are repositioned, including separating Figures 11 and 12 onto different pages, and printed page numbers disappear.

improvement.justification: The component ablations address missing evidence in v1, while the additional utility benchmarks and 13B evaluation strengthen empirical support for MANU. However, new Table 7 reports Idefics2 forget cloze values of 4.75 and 2.11 for vanilla/full MANU, conflicting with 44.75% and 32.11% in retained Tables 4–5. This unresolved inconsistency limits confidence in part of the added evidence and tempers the overall gain.
